entries.message:
Feature:<https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/ADP-3824| Support sending Stripe/Paddle events to integrations>
Release: September 3, 2026
Dependencies: Adjust, Amplitude, Mixpanel and Firebase
Effected areas: Events, Integrations

<!subteam^S03KC9S1QMC> <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <@U05QELDHUUX>

Sup, team - Stripe and Paddle purchases just landed in Adjust, Amplitude, Mixpanel and Firebase! :credit_card: :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Until today a Paddle purchase reached only AppsFlyer, Webhooks and PostHog, and no web purchase reached Adjust at all. Now both web stores send purchase events to all seven integrations, using the buyer’s mobile origin for attribution: install from an ad, pay on the website, and the purchase shows up next to the install in Adjust or Amplitude.

• Paddle now works in Amplitude, Mixpanel and Firebase the same way Stripe does, through separate Paddle keys in the integration settings
• Adjust gets web purchases for the first time, tied to the same device and campaign as the install

Who this is for: any customer with a web checkout, especially Stripe/Paddle apps on Adjust or AppsFlyer.

:warning: Paddle keys are not optional - empty key, dropped event. Adjust, AppsFlyer and Firebase skip buyers who never opened the app (no device ID). Facebook and custom stores are not in this release yet.

Huge kudos to: <@U0AQZG23D62> <@U0ACSQAKJA1>

P.S: I believe Josh from Wave and others who asked this feature will be very happy about it, <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> please let them know :heart_on_fire:

entries.name: Hey team, we’ve just launched a new feature for Adapty Attribution: Predicted LTV for Meta Ads.
entries.message:
Hey team, we’ve just launched a new feature for Adapty Attribution: Predicted LTV for Meta Ads.

Instead of sending Meta only the revenue a user generated today, Adapty can send the revenue that user is expected to generate over time.

For example, Meta might normally see:

Trial started: $0
First payment: $9.99

With Predicted LTV, Adapty can tell Meta: This user is expected to generate $45 over 90 days

This matters because Meta’s value optimization is only as good as the conversion values we give it. If we send only the first payment, Meta may optimize toward users who convert cheaply today, not necessarily the users who generate the most revenue over time.

Predicted LTV helps Meta optimize toward long-term subscriber value, not just the first transaction.

It also works naturally with Qualified Trials: Qualified Trials decides which users are worth sending. Predicted LTV tells Meta how much those users may be worth.

Adapty already has the subscription and retention data. Now customers can use that data directly for campaign optimization without building the entire prediction pipeline themselves.

Adapty Attribution is not only about measuring where users came from. We can also improve the quality and value of the signals ad networks use to optimize campaigns.

Together, Attribution + Qualified Trials + Predicted LTV gives us a much stronger signal engineering story for subscription apps.

entries.message:
hey team. last week we tinkered a lot and made a thing — a way to use the *flow builder for coding agents*.

now agents like claude code, cowork and codex can create and edit flows in adapty. and by edit i mean, you know, REAL edit — components, themes, locales, interactivity and everything else that's possible with our builder.

how it it's different from builder ai chat, and why it's important:
• *model ability* — chat: we own model selection and pay for tokens, so user can't use the smartest yet expensive model. skill: user brings his own model, so output quality is capped only by frontier model capabilities, not by adapty economy
• *freedom* — chat: curated selection of tools, more economical and safe, but restricted (no images, no locales, no working outside a single screen yet). skill: full freedom to the agent, whole flow config, no feature limit, better results, but more tokens burned and way less safe
• *look to the future* — chat: good starting point for normies. skill: canvas for pioneers, and i believe we can take inspiration from our most creative skill power users to improve both builder and ai chat
_nb_: it's powerful but risky — agents can upload broken configs (we validate + preview, but still). use and recommend with caution.

give it a shot, folks! open your code/cowork/codex and:
1. ask to install the `flow-generator` skill using `npx skills@latest add adaptyteam/adapty-skills`; more ways <https://adapty.io/docs/flow-generator-skill#install-the-skill|here>
2. run `/flow-generator`, ask to create some gorgeous flow
3. share the result to the thread. go go power rangers!
shoutout to <@U08QUJMN0UV> <@U080G9FHV50> <@U08JY3U9S7P>

entries.message:
Hey everyone! Here's what's been going on with AdaptyMail and why it's been quiet for so long:
*we stand on the Amazon review*

In July Amazon put our sending account under review. While it's open, billing is frozen and we're not onboarding new clients. If we don't clear it, they cut off sending, and without sending there's no product.
The main complaint was about links. A single email pulled them from four different places: some pointed at the client's domain, some at ours, some straight to the App Store, some at Amazon's own tracking addresses. To a spam filter that looks like an email assembled from parts of unclear origin. On top of that, link reputation is scored separately from sender reputation, so one client with a bad list was dragging down the link domains for everyone else.
We've built everything they asked for, and we're sending our response to the review team *today*.

What we did with links
Every client now gets their own link subdomain, something like <http://go.theirdomain.com|go.theirdomain.com>. During setup the client adds one DNS record pointing at us, plus a second housekeeping record so the security certificate renews automatically and nobody has to touch it every three months. From there, every link in the email, all of them, runs through that subdomain.
Then it splits. Images live in our Cloudflare storage and get served directly, no hop involved: the reader sees the client's address, the image comes from us, nobody notices anything.

Clicks work differently. The request reaches us, we record the event, and we send the person on to wherever they were going. The address bar stays on the client's domain the whole time, and nobody ever gets bounced through a domain of ours.
Click tracking is ours now, not Amazon's. Their built-in tracking rewrote links to their own addresses, and those addresses were exactly the foreign element in the email. We turned it off and replaced it with our own. As a side benefit, click data now sits with us instead of in someone else's system with their format and their delay.

What else we did
Email confirmation is live. When an email address shows up on a user, they get a message with a button. Until they press it, no marketing goes out. We built it so a mail provider's security scanner can't press it for them, which happens more often than you'd think and wrecks both the numbers and the point of the whole thing.

We split two things apart: whether an address is confirmed, and whether the person agreed to marketing. The first applies to all mail, service messages included. The second only to marketing, and the person ticks that box themselves in the app.
Each client now gets stopped on their own. If complaints spike for one client, sending pauses for that client and everyone else keeps running. Before, one dirty list could taint everyone's reputation at once.

Next: we wait for Amazon's answer. Once the review lifts, billing and new client onboarding unfreeze.

*Another big thing: FunnelFox integration is live today!*
FunnelFox runs the funnel that takes a user from the web into the app. Adapty Mail now handles the email at every step of it.
Leads from FunnelFox reach us immediately, with nothing for the client to export and nothing to configure on their side. People are split by where they stalled: dropped the quiz, reached checkout and didn't buy, paid and never installed. All three used to get the same email. Now each gets their own.
For clients already on FunnelFox, it's running.

Experiment ID identifies the specific funnel someone came through, and a specific funnel is a specific audience. *We've significantly upgraded our prediction model in cohorts*

Release: August 17
Affected areas: Analytics (Cohorts)

Highlights:
• 2–3× more accurate predictions, with especially large gains for young cohorts in their first month.
• Added predictions for lifetime subscriptions and one-time purchases, consistent with recurring subscriptions.
• Predictions now kick in at just 30 subscriptions, down from 100.
Under the hood, it remains a fully interpretable model: it learns revenue and subscriber gains between consecutive day-checkpoints from the start of each cohort, with careful calibration and a few tricks in between.

Kudos to <@U0AJS52CDS4>

*We've significantly upgraded our prediction model in cohorts*

Release: August 17
Affected areas: Analytics (Cohorts)

Highlights:
• 2–3× more accurate predictions, with especially large gains for young cohorts in their first month.
• Added predictions for lifetime subscriptions and one-time purchases, consistent with recurring subscriptions.
• Predictions now kick in at just 30 subscriptions, down from 100.
Under the hood, it remains a fully interpretable model: it learns revenue and subscriber gains between consecutive day-checkpoints from the start of each cohort, with careful calibration and a few tricks in between.

Kudos to <@U0AJS52CDS4>

Heads-up for the <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ>: some predictions shift significantly (20%+), mostly upward.

Why predictions can shift:
• The new model better captures conversions that don't happen close to the install date. The size of the shift strongly correlates with cohort age: younger cohorts change most, while for older cohorts the two models converge to almost zero difference.
• Lifetime subscriptions and one-time purchases used to show actual revenue as the prediction. Now they grow the same way other products do.
Also FYI, first predictions are available once the install period has fully elapsed and the longest possible trial from that period has had time to convert.

entries.message:
:rocket: *Launching today: Search Popularity + Keyword Suggester*

We are bringing the keyword discovery stage into Adapty.
*Search Popularity* shows ranked App Store search terms for a selected market, genre, and completed period. *Keyword Suggester* expands a seed into related phrase candidates and Apple category context, then helps users build a shortlist.
Together, they replace an unstructured mix of intuition, spreadsheets, and external tools with a transparent workflow based on Apple-provided signals. This is useful for Apple Ads research, ASO, market expansion, and product positioning — and it creates the foundation for future recommendation and campaign-building workflows.
Important: popularity is a relative research signal, not search volume, conversion, or a performance forecast.
Please try both releases with a real use case and share feedback on relevance, clarity, and the next action you would expect after building a shortlist.

entries.message:
Hey team, we’ve been working on a new feature for Adapty Attribution, and it’s now live: Qualified Trials.

With Qualified Trials, customers can choose to send trial events to Meta and TikTok only after a user has stayed in the trial for a defined number of hours without cancelling.

So instead of sending every trial start as a signal, Adapty can send only the higher-quality trial events. This helps customers improve signal quality, reduce noise, and give ad networks better data for campaign optimization.

We can use it to talk about:
• Better signal engineering for subscription apps
• Higher-quality optimization events for Meta campaigns
• Reducing noisy trial signals
• Helping UA teams optimize for users with stronger purchase intent
It’s live on the dashboard. cc <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ>

Big thanks to <@U08PXEX7CAK> for implementing this so quickly

Feature: <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/ADP-6445|Apple Retention Messaging API>
Release: July 30, 2026 (under feature flag)
Dependencies: None
Effected areas: Dashboard (new section), Analytics

<!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <!subteam^S03KC9S1QMC> <@U05QELDHUUX> <@U06K36L6CTB>

Sup, team — it’s finally here (under feature flag BUT goes live this week)! :apple:

When a subscriber taps Cancel Subscription in iOS Settings, Apple now shows _your_ message right in the cancellation sheet — a value reminder, a discount, or a plan switch — before the cancellation is confirmed. The one screen apps never owned, now addressable straight from Adapty:

• on-device preview — see the message in Apple’s cancel sheet (light & dark) before it goes to review (Our benefit, only SW support)
• AI localization — write once in English, auto translate fills every locale. (Our benefit, RC and SW doesn’t support this)
• save-rate analytics — Shown / Saved / Save rate per message
Apple’s side is still in beta, so we’re shipping behind a feature flag purely as a safety net. Until it comes off, enable it in the browser console:
`window.adapty_ff.set('retentionMessaging', true)` → Apple Retention Messaging appears in the left nav. Poke around and drop anything odd in this thread. <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> You can provide it to your clients who are approved from Apple, most probably we’ll disable it this week and go LIVE!

*Who this is for:* 
Any iOS subscription app that wants to lift retention with zero engineering - no endpoint, no SDK update. Sharpest fits: price-sensitive apps (discount at cancel intent), monthly + annual mixes (plan switch instead of churn).

*What’s next:* 
Analytics improvements (adding saved $ metric), then A/B testing if adoption is strong.

Docs: <https://adapty.io/docs/retention-messaging|adapty.io/docs/retention-messaging>

Huge kudos to <@U0ACSQAKJA1> <@U09AH7D2A4X> <@U0AQZG23D62> <@U0A3M160RB4> <@U08ASB4GYR4> <@U0AKC1Y09R8> :fire:

entries.message:
*AI Agent (Apple Ads) - what two months of client conversations tell us*

I've analyzed every client conversation with the agent since release. In this post, I'll share the main highlights. You can find the full analysis in the document: <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-18-27-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|:bar_chart: AI Agent Chat Analytics> + interactive visualization attached.

*The numbers*:
• 81 client orgs tried the agent → 221 real chats
• *72% of orgs (58) started one chat and never came back* :epic-sad:
• 11 deep sessions with 10+ messages - clients execute its instructions step by step and come back for verification.
*What separates those who stayed from those who left:*
• Churned clients opened with broad questions - "what's wrong with my ads?" in various forms. The agent answered, couldn't create or change anything itself, and the client never returned.
• Retained clients came with specific tasks - "what's up with my ROAS?" - which gives them a reason to come back and re-check regularly. One client literally runs the same weekly-report prompt every Monday across 3–4 apps, polishing it a bit each iteration.
*Potential agent improvements:*
1. Scheduled reports/checks - "check my ROAS every Monday."
2. Agent-initiated follow-ups - client asks "what can I improve?", agent gives recommendations and offers: "Want me to re-check in 3 days and ping you?" with an "Ok, remind me" button. Should lift retention for clients who come with broad questions.
Attached to the message is a visualization of the analytics in the form of an HTML file.
You can also find an MD file with analytics <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-Agent-Chat-Analytics-May-25-July-28-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|in the Document>.

sup, team

last month we've been cooking an *ai agent* for our one and only *flow builder*. it can do (almost) everything you can do via the ui — add and edit elements, styles and copy; and since it's powered by claude, it can mimic well-known app styles, suggest layouts according to best practices, etc.

today we're ready for an *internal release*. it was a rough ride and we're still not quite there. we're working hard on polishing, and you can help us shape the path to public release. it's easy — if you're building a new gorgeous flow and tempted to use ui buttons, just tell yourself "oh man, it's the year 2026 and i'm doing something old-school and not burning tokens. i need to change my life and fast"

so, here is the way:
1. open any flow on any app
2. open the browser console and enter the command: `adapty_ff.set('FLOW_GENERATOR', true)`
3. now instead of editing flow manually, open the chat using :sparkles: button in the left sidebar and type (or dictate) what you desire to do
4. notice what works well, what's not, what's missing and write in down to this thread. we'll take care of it
known restrictions: it's not always the smartest, it works on a per-screen basis, it leaks config internals and sometimes it may crash the page :this_is_fine: . we're working on it, stay tuned.

shoutout and love to <@U08EVBTE69E> <@U07PR2368G5> <@U0ALSG3VA30> <@U080G9FHV50> <@U08JY3U9S7P>

Feature: <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/ADP-5994|Virtual currencies support>
Release date: July 21, 2026

<!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <!subteam^S03KC9S1QMC> <@U05QELDHUUX> <@U06K36L6CTB> It’s finally here! :money-smell:

You can now define in-app currencies - credits, tokens, coins - link them to your products, and Adapty will automatically grant and track balances for every user.

*Who this is for:*
• *AI apps* - charge credits per generation, bundle a monthly allowance into subscriptions, sell credit packs as one-time products
• *Short drama / video apps* - coins to unlock episodes
• *Games* - soft + hard currency with atomic conversions
• *Education & productivity* - hearts, lives, metered actions like OCR or exports
*How it works:*
Сreate a currency, map it to products with credit amounts, and every purchase or renewal credits the user automatically. Reading and spending balances happens through the *server-side API.* 

*What’s next:*
If adoption is strong, we’re planning Flow Builder support (analogue of product variables), manual credits from the dashboard, SDK methods, and balance-based segments to target paywalls.

Docs: <https://adapty.io/docs/virtual-currencies|adapty.io/docs/virtual-currencies>

Huge kudos to: <@U08ASB4GYR4> <@U09AH7D2A4X> <@U0A3M160RB4> <@U0AQZG23D62> <@U0AKC1Y09R8>

hey team,

need some help with Readability who is evaluating RC needs some answers and ready to sign now if we can give the right AND ACCURATE responses.

i go into more detail but overall they feel like the onboarding is a incomplete product, and that RC, has a great onboarding and paywall builder in comparison to us. this goes against all internal dialogue so i hope we can turn these questions into feedback and action items.

quick background:

• legacy reading/education app
• 21k+ 5-star reviews
• ~$250k MRR today
• existing FunnelFox customer
• evaluating Adapty vs RevenueCat (RC is "more mature and has a better onboarding builder" 
• expects to scale roughly 2-2.5x before the end of 2026
they are already invested in FunnelFox and want to stay in our ecosystem if we can confidently answer a few questions. details all below:

<@U9HDNS9S4>

• does the new onboarding builder support sign in/sign up with Apple, Google, Facebook, email, and existing account login?
• can they place authentication both before and after the paywall within the onboarding flow?
• can they make API calls during onboarding and write/read data from their backend?
• will custom HTML/script support be available in the new onboarding builder and when?
• how confident are we that Android support for the onboarding builder ships in early July?
• what is the status and ETA for React Native integration with flow builder ?
<@U9HDNS9S4> / <@U0AGF7L13L5>

• RC has Amazon support and they sell on amazon, is this on our road map. when? 
• what is the status and ETA for Apple Retention Messaging?
they also have concerns stemming from their FunnelFox implementation and the Braintree workarounds they had to build.
need clarity on:


• entitlement management for Braintree subscriptions
• app access for Braintree subscribers
• analytics visibility
• can Braintree subscriptions be imported and used for entitlement/access management inside Adapty?
• how historical Braintree subscription data would be migrated
• engineering lift required
• known limitations
<@U08EVBTE69E>

RevenueCat was positioned as having a massive template library and a more mature onboarding platform.

they brought templates up multiple times throughout the call as a way to reduce implementation time and get to best practices faster.

• when can we realistically expect onboarding templates?
• when could we realistically promise onboarding templates for children's education/reading apps?
one additional note:

they only plan to run 3 onboarding/paywall flows initially.

if we can answer the questions above and get those first few flows stood up, I think we win this deal. PS is obviously slammed, but I don't think we need a huge engagement here to get them over the finish line.

<@U074DLWC5L7> <@U08MPLZ50NP> if we cannot have templates and SSO and everything else they need would it be possible to build 1-3 funnels and paywalls for them? this is a RC head to head and will be over 500MRR in less than 6 months.

appreciate any guidance.

cc: <@U034A27SVHC> if you would like to join the call i added you as optional

Hi there! I suppose sometimes core-related posts will look less like a cool new feature for customers. So, this is a story about an invisible defensive feature: the kind that hopefully no customer ever notices, because its whole purpose is to prevent bad things from happening in the background.
It was implemented and delivered a sprint ago, but I believe that late is better than never.

*What's the deal?* 
The main problem this feature revolves around is "Forwarding event loops".
Adapty allows its users to forward events into third-party systems for further processing and that's perfectly fine - many customers, especially big ones use it. However, the issue is that we have no control over what our customers do in other systems in terms of event routing. And rarely, but very painfully we encountered situations where some of our customers were configuring third-party systems in a way that forwarded events further... back to Adapty.
Easy to guess, what happened next: reforward back to them, receive again, repeat until (almost) forever (but most likely until something breaks under the load). So given that, if someone configured back-forwarding and experienced a spike of events (say a lot of transactions in a short period of time) - we're cooked, just like Spider-Man's "no you!" meme but on high speed. Why is it bad? Well, apart from useless load on our metal, we had already experienced a few painful downtimes of the integrations pipeline because of it.

*Aha, and what you did?*
To prevent this, we added a small layer of event analysis on the fly for the integrations flow: before forwarding, we decompose an event in a store-based manner (separately App Store v1, v2 and Play Store), combine some of its data into `deduplication key` - like a passport for an event and store it in memory for an hour at the moment of forwarding. If an App Store / Play Store related event is about to be forwarded and its deduplication key is already present, we simply do nothing integration-wise. That's it.
We shipped it in two stages: for the first week, we just added a few logs/notifications around such suspicious passengers, to see if it worked at all. Surprising discoveries around it were that even at this stage there were a few really small customers with such loops. Only around 1-2 transactions per day, but still buzzing every minute or so on constant ping-ponging events back and forth. The second stage, obviously, was about transforming alerts into strict bans on forwarding.
We haven’t had a real forward-storm since then, which is good news, but the mechanism is already catching small misconfigurations.

Big thanks go to <@U04B26DSWMA> for implementing the first version, <@U0AR243M9T9> for the initial review, and <@UNWFN144R> for the review battle that helped make this thing nice and robust.

*P.S.* We’re a bit behind with this feed, but next week we’ll catch up and share a few more recent releases - about integrations, billing, and the initial work on Virtual Currencies and Apple Retention Messaging API.
